$comment: GENERATED FILE -- the expectations below are emitted by Go. Do not hand-edit them.
Go is the source of truth for indexability. services/worker/internal/seourl.Decide
is the authority; this file is its output, and the web page is tested against it.
Why this exists. Indexability is necessarily decided twice: the worker sweep
decides what the sitemap advertises, and the fixture page decides its own robots
tag. Neither can call the other -- one is Go on a schedule, the other TypeScript
on a request -- so nothing structural kept them in step. On 2026-09-28 they went
out of step: the history gate was flagged on the sweep but applied unconditionally
on the page, and the sitemap advertised 136 URLs the page served as noindex.
The repo already pinned the shared CONSTANTS across this boundary. It did not pin
the shared DECISION, which is where divergence actually happens. Now a change to
Decide regenerates this file, the TypeScript test fails until the page agrees, and
the mismatch is caught before merge rather than by a post-deploy audit that samples
400 of 16,730 URLs against a cached sitemap.
goOnly marks cases the page cannot evaluate because the input is not on its
payload: duplicate resolution is a catalogue concern the sweep owns alone.

cases.name: upcoming fixture with a prediction and history on both sides
no prediction is the largest excluded population
recently settled fixture still carries search demand
aged out well past the archive threshold
fractional days past the threshold still archive (14.16d once advertised a retired page)
just inside the threshold is still indexable
one side thin still withholds -- the preview can say nothing about half the match
exactly at the bar on both sides is indexable
one short on the away side
a match on the pitch is never archived however old its kickoff reads
unknown status past kickoff is not concluded, so it does not archive
archived outranks thin history -- only one of the two is recoverable
postponed ages out like any other concluded status
a duplicate is never advertised whatever else is true of it
